takeaways: Miami's landmark land deal: Ken Griffin paid $1.1B all-cash (about $37M/acre) for Moishe Mana's 30-acre Wynwood assemblage to anchor a $2B Carnegie Mellon campus, on top of his $2.5B Citadel HQ in Brickell.
Senior housing occupancy topped 90% in Q3, with more than half of primary markets at 90%+, while construction runs about 10,445 units a year against 100,000+ needed to keep pace.

Financing stress is building: MBS ETFs saw $2.4B of outflows in September (the most since March 2020) with Treasuries above 5%, and California seized $690M CRE-heavy Nano Banc, the sixth U.S. bank failure of 2026.

items.headline: Ken Griffin pays $1.1B all-cash for Mana's Wynwood assemblage for CMU Miami
items.summary: Ken Griffin's $3B gift to Carnegie Mellon includes $2B for a new 35-acre CMU campus in Miami's Wynwood. Its core is a 30-acre parcel he bought from Moishe Mana for $1.1B (about $37M/acre) in an all-cash, no-broker deal nearly three years in the making, versus the roughly $70M Mana spent assembling it. Griffin is also building a $2.5B Citadel HQ in Brickell, adding another major demand driver to Miami. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Senior housing occupancy tops 90% as half of primary markets hit 90%+
items.summary: NIC MAP data shows senior housing occupancy surpassed 90% in Q3 2026, near a record, with more than half of primary markets averaging 90% or higher (Boston at 94.0%). Sustaining 90% occupancy would take more than 100,000 new units a year through the late 2030s, but construction is averaging only about 10,445 units a year, roughly a tenth of what's needed.

items.headline: California seizes Nano Banc, sixth U.S. bank failure of 2026
items.summary: California's DFPI seized Nano Banc, a $690M CRE-heavy lender that the Fed had been pushing to cut its CRE loan concentration since 2021; Utah-based Sunwest Bank is taking over its deposits. The bank was tied to Mahender Makhijani's alleged Continuum Analytics fraud scheme, which also hit Western Alliance and Zions. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Mortgage bond ETFs see biggest outflows since March 2020
items.summary: Investors pulled $2.4B from U.S. mortgage-backed securities ETFs in September, the biggest monthly outflow since March 2020, led by about $2.7B leaving BlackRock's iShares MBS ETF. With Treasury yields above 5%, investors are favoring simpler Treasuries over MBS. That pressures mortgage spreads and could push up borrowing costs across housing and real estate finance.

items.headline: JPMorgan weighs $3.8B construction loan for Extell's Upper West Side supertall
items.summary: JPMorgan is in talks to lead a roughly $3.8B construction loan for Extell's 1,200-foot luxury condo tower on West 66th Street, the former ABC headquarters site that Gary Barnett bought for $930M in 2022. It would rank among the largest construction loans ever made in the U.S., a sign of lender confidence in ultra-luxury residential while Manhattan's condo pipeline sits at a low of about 2,800 new units.

items.headline: Ex-SL Green exec's GreenBarn buys $250M note on SLG's Olivia rental
items.summary: GreenBarn, the venture of former SL Green co-CIO David Schonbraun, bought the note on the Olivia, SLG's 333-unit Penn Plaza rental. The 10-year, 4.2% fixed loan had an original principal of $250M (about $500/sf); it is reportedly performing but matures at the end of February, a test of how 2017-vintage multifamily debt refinances at today's rates. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Apartment pipeline is more concentrated than metro data suggests
items.summary: The top 10 multifamily permitting metros issued 150,614 permits in the 12 months through August, up 25% year-over-year, led by New York (36,496), Los Angeles (17,926), Dallas (15,924) and Houston (13,772). Florida is mixed: Miami permits fell by 2,219 and Orlando by 3,496, while West Palm Beach rose by 2,502. City-level permits also cluster heavily in urban cores, so metro-wide totals can understate submarket supply risk.

items.headline: Mega deals are distorting CRE's comeback numbers
items.summary: MSCI data shows August CRE volume was inflated by mega M&A such as the Equity Residential-AvalonBay merger forming Vivmark, while individual property sales fell 28% year-over-year in August. Prices rose just 0.1% year-over-year, pointing to a slower, more gradual recovery than headline volume suggests.

items.headline: SNF owner RegalCare pays $1M to settle overbilling as expansion draws scrutiny
items.summary: NJ-based skilled nursing operator RegalCare, owner Eli Mirlis and an executive agreed to pay $1M to settle U.S. Attorney allegations of overbilling Medicare and Massachusetts Medicaid. A Boston Globe investigation found Mirlis cut nursing spending at a Taunton facility by about $530K while his real estate company raised its rent to $522K, more than four times the prior level, a sharp example of the regulatory risk in operator-landlord structures. (via The Promote)

items.headline: CBRE: U.S. could run out of prime office space by end of 2027
items.summary: CBRE says only 5% of office workers are highly vulnerable to AI displacement and attributes slower job growth mainly to demographics (about 83,000 retirements a month). Tech firms made up 21% of U.S. office leasing in H1 2026, mostly in the Bay Area and Manhattan, and with new construction collapsing, the U.S. could exhaust prime space by the end of 2027.

items.headline: CPOs at HPE, Palo Alto, Lennar: AI has 'killed the org chart'
items.summary: At Fortune's AIQ summit, people chiefs from HPE, Palo Alto Networks and Lennar said AI is flattening traditional hierarchies. Palo Alto's internal AI agent cut IT tickets by 83% and lets employees self-serve HR questions, and the companies now hire for curiosity and adaptability over credentials. Lennar's CHRO said upskilling is increasingly the employee's responsibility.

items.headline: JLL CEO Christian Ulbrich: 'The core place for work is the office'
items.summary: JLL CEO Christian Ulbrich argues in-office work is more efficient and essential for learning, since skills from university go stale within about three years. He says offices must be attractive enough to earn attendance. JLL rose to No. 175 on the Fortune 500 after posting 11% Q2 revenue growth and raising guidance.

items.headline: Ford and JPMorgan back $2B push to close the skilled-trades gap
items.summary: Ford and JPMorgan are teaming up on a $2B initiative to train skilled trades workers as the U.S. faces demand for about 1.7 million trades workers a year. Carhartt's CEO notes trades can pay 32% more, though schools still steer Gen Z away, a talent dynamic that affects construction and property maintenance staffing.

items.headline: Dubai targets $9.5B from longevity as Oura postpones its IPO
items.summary: Dubai's new Longevity Authority aims to add more than Dh35B (about $9.5B) to the emirate's economy over the next decade, as longevity investment spreads across Asia and the Middle East. Smart-ring maker Oura postponed its U.S. IPO amid volatile markets, and sauna and heat-therapy culture keeps gaining momentum.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley commits $684M to Uptown Dallas hub
items.summary: Morgan Stanley will anchor a 700,000 SF Trammell Crow tower at 2401 McKinney Ave. under a 16-year lease starting in 2031 and take 255,000 SF at Fountain Place in the interim, targeting 3,800 Dallas employees by 2035. The hub sits about a mile from Goldman Sachs' $709M Uptown campus, concentrating premium finance demand in Uptown.

items.headline: RoseVilla plans next evolution with three major development projects
items.summary: Portland-area nonprofit operator RoseVilla is planning three major development projects to expand its campus, another sign that operators are moving to add supply as occupancy tightens nationally.

items.headline: Touchmark breaks ground in Alaska; Cedarhurst hits milestones in Illinois, Kansas
items.summary: Touchmark has started construction on a new senior living project in Alaska, and Cedarhurst reached development milestones in Illinois and Kansas, adding to the small but growing wave of new senior living starts.

items.headline: The rise of the two-job worker: 61% now do more than one role
items.summary: Fortune reports that 61% of workers now do more than one role, and a Goldman Sachs retirement survey finds about 8 in 10 Gen Z and millennial workers hold two jobs because of affordability pressures. The trend matters for frontline staffing and retention.

items.headline: Full-body health scans boom as Magic AI raises $11M for fitness mirror
items.summary: Full-body health scans are booming despite debate over whether they're necessary, longevity services are going global, and AI fitness-mirror startup Magic AI raised $11M.
